newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO's Arafat hosts Peres as Arabs shun Netanyahu.
newsitem.headline: PLO's Arafat hosts Peres as Arabs shun Netanyahu.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat hosted Israeli opposition leader Shimon Peres in the West Bank on Sunday as Israel's Arab friends warned Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu not to tamper with peace accords.

Arafat and Peres met in self-ruled Nablus, the last West Bank town still under an Israeli blockade imposed after fierce clashes killed 60 Palestinians and 15 Israelis in September, to discuss now-threatened peace deals the two men crafted.

Israeli and U.S. officials said later on Sunday talks on a long-postponed army redeployment from the West Bank town of Hebron, which were to have convened in Egypt's Red Sea resort of Taba on Monday, had been delayed one day.

"We are here now to follow up...how we shall protect the peace process, how we shall defend it and how we shall push it forward in this difficult situation," Arafat said after the meeting at Israel's former occupation headquarters, now the Governate of autonomous Nablus.
Asked if he had carried a message to the Palestinian leader, Peres told reporters with a smile: "I am the message."
The Nobel peace laureates met as Israel's Arab peace partners gave a cold shoulder to the right-wing Netanyahu, who put peace moves on ice after ousting Peres in May.

Israeli relations with Egypt, Jordan and the Palestinians have deteriorated as Netanyahu has stalled implementation of an already long-delayed Israeli redeployment from the West Bank town of Hebron agreed more than a year ago.
The overdue troop pullback is the central issue in U.S.-brokered peace talks.
PLO negotiator Saeb Erekat said the talks with Netanyahu's government had yielded "not one inch of progress". He urged Washington to push Israel to honour the Hebron deal.

Arab leaders made a point of extending invitations to Labour party head Peres and Israeli President Ezer Weizman while excluding Netanyahu. Peres was summoned to Nablus by Arafat and to Egypt by President Hosni Mubarak next week.

Weizman, whose job is largely ceremonial, was due on Monday in Egypt where he is seen as an elder statesman in contrast with the young and less experienced Netanyahu. Weizman was due in Jordan sometime next week.

Mubarak said on Saturday that he refused to meet Netanyahu until Israel solved the Hebron issue with the Palestinians. "The situation is still complicated. There's no (Israeli) commitment to what was agreed," Mubarak told reporters.

Jordan, Israel's warmest Arab friend since a 1994 peace treaty, echoed Egypt's pessimism. Jordanian Information Minister Marwan Muasher said on Sunday that Israel "not only lacked a desire to implement accords, but what is more dangerous...a call to open all files of past accords (peace)."
Arafat was expected to travel to Amman on Monday to brief Jordan's King Hussein on progress in U.S.-brokered peace talks on implementation of the Hebron troop pullback.
The Hebron redeployment should have been carried out in March but was delayed by Peres after Islamic militant suicide bombers killed 59 people in Israel in February and March.

It was frozen by Netanyahu, who says the deal must be changed to ensure the security of 400 Jewish settlers living in enclaves amid 100,000 Arabs in Hebron. Palestinians refuse to amend the Hebron accord they signed with the former government.
Peres, asked whether he was sorry he had not implemented the Hebron deal, quipped: "I regret that I didn't win the election."
Peres urged patience while talks continued. "Despite the difficulties and despite the disappointments, peace is not dead. We shall overcome this crisis and we shall go ahead." he said.
"You should not lose hope," Peres said to Arafat.
